messages.subject: Rhipe: Reading opentsdb data
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run mapreduce using hbase database. I am trying to read tsdb table. I already have set of rowkeys.

Is there any function in Rhipe rhmr(), where I can send data in distributed mode, rather than saving in hdfs filesystem.


/***********Function to get data from hbase table***********************/
 getdata <- function(x,handle=tb){
    lapply( handle$get(x,what='course:math'),function(r)
 rhuz(r$"course:math"))
   }

/**********************************************************************/


z <- rhwatch(rhmr(map=m,  reduce=r,  inout=c("sequence", "sequence"), mapred=getdata("b","c"),param=list(F=F),N=20))  //map reduce function where "b","c" are row keys


Does sending data directly to mapred parameter will work?

Is there anything else I can do to send data to mapreduce task.

Any kind of help on this would be highly appreciable.

Regards
Bikas

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Rhipe: Reading opentsdb data
parts:
by any chance, are you using rhbase? Assuming you have that package working,
Code that worked for me:
library(rJava)
library(rbase)
hb <- rb.init()
crashers <- rb.table.new(hb,"crash.signatures",model, meta, additional)
   
setup <- expression(map={
  library(rJava)
  library(rbase)
  hb <- rb.init()                                    
  crasher <- rb.table.connect(hb,"crash.signatures")
  rhsz <- function (x) .Call("rh_sz",x); rhuz <- function(x) .Call("rh_uz",x)
})
m <- rhmap({
  res = crasher$get(rowkey,"model:data")[[1]]$"model:data"
  crasher$putOne(k[[1]], values=list("model:data"=r,'meta:dummy'=TRUE)) ## because of bug, need at least two names
})
res <- rhwatch(rhmr(map=m, reduce=0,setup=setup,ifolder='beta15.smz'))

If you are using rbase, be prepared to work alone. It is not supported and very alpha.
The hoops you have to jump through (look at the setup) is because of a design flaw in RHIPE which will be fixed 0.74

Regards
Saptarshi

Sorry, in above code might be some mistake, Here is the final code I am using

Code:

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()

hbasemap <- function(tablename, colspec, rows,caching=3L, cacheBlocks=TRUE){
  ## This function can be used when ever accessing Hbase

mapred <- list()
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.tablename <- as.character(tablename[1])
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.colspec <- paste(colspec,collapse=",")
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.start <-rows[1]
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.rowlim.end <- rows[2]

mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.cacheblocks <- sprintf("%s:%s",as.integer(caching),as.integer(cacheBlocks))
  mapred$rhipe.hbase.mozilla.prefix <- "byteprefix"
  mapred$rhipe_inputformat_class <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHCrashReportTableInputFormat'
  mapred$rhipe_inputformat_keyclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.RHBytesWritable'
  mapred$rhipe_inputformat_valueclass <- 'org.godhuli.rhipe.hbase.RHResult'
  mapred
}



####Map function to get key and value#######################
map <- expression({
   lapply(seq_along(map.values), function(r) {
      v <- map.values[[r]]

      k <- map.keys[[r]]
      rhcollect(k, mean(v))
   })
})

#######Reduce function to sort and shuffle######################
reduce <- expression(
   pre={
      mean <- 0
  
   },
 reduce={
      mean <- max(mean, unlist(reduce.values))
   },
   post={
      rhcollect(reduce.key, mean)
   }
  
)
########################################################

result <- rhwatch(map        = map
                ,reduce    = reduce,
                ,input     = hbasemap(table="scores" ,colspec="course:art", c("a","b"))

,debug     = 'count'
                ,param     = list(beginningOflastMonth = Sys.Date()-45))

parts: Hello,
>could we define row-key and leave column qualifier null.

If you download (updated now) :
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RhipeHbaseMozilla/blob/master/java/rhipecrashreport.jar?raw=true
then you can set colspec="" and you get all col families and column

Your rowkey is a string. Is this a Java string? HBase stores rowkeys as raw bytes

- if the key is a string, hbaseif converts it to bytes using charToRaw
- otherwise the key *must* be a raw vector - it is upto the user to convert it to raw bytes

so rowkey (and *use argument names* in the function call)
hbaseif(..., rows=list(key1,key2))
